title: AC Repair
description: Understand common air-conditioning problems, the checks a repair visit may involve, and how proposed work can be explained before you decide.
listing_description: Cooling, airflow, drainage and operating issues for split and window air conditioners.

common_problems.title: Running but not cooling
common_problems.description: The unit turns on, but the room stays warm or takes longer than usual to cool.

common_problems.title: Water around the indoor unit
common_problems.description: Drips or damp patches may be associated with drainage, installation or other issues.

common_problems.title: Unusual noise or smell
common_problems.description: Rattling, buzzing or a musty odour can be useful details to share before inspection.

common_problems.title: Weak airflow or frequent stops
common_problems.description: Low airflow, short cycling or difficulty starting may need an in-person assessment.

inspection_scope: Discuss symptoms, recent changes and the unit type or model.
Inspect accessible filters, airflow, drainage and visible connections as appropriate.
Explain findings and outline any recommended work before parts or additional labour are considered.
Record the agreed scope and any customer-approved changes in the service notes.

questions.question: Why might an AC run without cooling well?
questions.answer: Possible causes range from restricted airflow to electrical or refrigerant-system issues. A symptom description cannot confirm the cause; an inspection is needed before recommending repair.

questions.question: Should I clean the filter before an inspection?
questions.answer: You can check the manufacturer guidance for your model and clean only parts intended for user maintenance. Do not open electrical or refrigerant components.

questions.question: Does an estimate include replacement parts?
questions.answer: A clear estimate should list inspection, labour and any proposed parts separately where applicable. Ask for the scope to be explained before approving work.

title: Refrigerator Repair
description: Explore refrigerator symptoms, useful information to share, and the checks that may be discussed before repair work is proposed.
listing_description: Cooling, frost, water, noise and power symptoms for refrigerators and freezers.

common_problems.title: Fridge or freezer is not cold enough
common_problems.description: Food compartments feel warmer than expected or temperatures vary through the day.

common_problems.title: Excess frost or ice build-up
common_problems.description: Ice collects around the freezer compartment, vents or door area.

common_problems.title: Water pooling nearby
common_problems.description: Water appears inside the cabinet, under a drawer or on the floor near the appliance.

common_problems.title: Clicking, buzzing or no power
common_problems.description: Share when the sound occurs and whether the display, lights or cooling have changed.

inspection_scope: Review the appliance type, model label and the symptoms you have noticed.
Check accessible controls, airflow paths, door seals and visible connections as appropriate.
Explain inspection findings and separate recommended parts from labour in a proposed estimate.
Request approval before any work outside the agreed scope is started.

questions.question: What details help describe a cooling problem?
questions.answer: Note which compartment is affected, when the issue began, any unusual sounds, and whether the door was left open or power was interrupted. These details do not replace an inspection.

questions.question: Can I keep using a refrigerator that is making a new sound?
questions.answer: Some operating sounds are normal, but a sudden or persistent change can be worth checking. If you notice smoke, a burning smell or damaged wiring, stop using it if safe and seek qualified help.

questions.question: Will replacement parts be included in the first estimate?
questions.answer: A part should be identified and listed separately when it is known. If diagnosis reveals additional work, the proposed change should be explained for your approval first.

title: Washing Machine Repair
description: Find common washer and spin-cycle symptoms, learn what a service inspection may cover, and see how a proposed repair can be itemised.
listing_description: Drain, spin, fill, vibration and leak concerns for common washing-machine types.

common_problems.title: Water does not drain
common_problems.description: Water remains in the drum after a cycle or the machine pauses before spinning.

common_problems.title: Drum will not spin
common_problems.description: A cycle completes without a normal spin, or clothes remain unusually wet.

common_problems.title: Excessive movement or noise
common_problems.description: The machine vibrates, knocks or shifts position more than expected during a cycle.

common_problems.title: Leaking or not filling
common_problems.description: Water appears around a hose or door, or the drum does not fill as expected.

inspection_scope: Confirm the washer type, visible error code and the point in the cycle where the issue occurs.
Inspect accessible hoses, drainage points, levelling and user controls as appropriate.
Explain the likely scope and distinguish labour from any proposed replacement parts.
Document the agreed work and ask before proceeding with any additional repair.

questions.question: What should I note before a washing-machine inspection?
questions.answer: If safe, note the cycle, load size, any displayed error code, and whether the issue occurs while filling, washing, draining or spinning. Do not remove panels or reach into a powered appliance.

questions.question: Could an unbalanced load cause vibration?
questions.answer: An uneven load or an unlevel machine can contribute to movement, but other causes are possible. Follow the appliance manual and share when the vibration happens.

questions.question: Are hoses and parts included in a repair estimate?
questions.answer: The estimate should make clear what inspection and labour cover, and list any proposed parts separately when applicable. Additional work should be presented for approval.

title: RO Water Purifier Repair
description: Learn about common water-purifier symptoms and the checks a technician may discuss, without treating a symptom as a confirmed diagnosis.
listing_description: Low water flow, unusual taste, leaks and indicator issues for RO water purifiers.

common_problems.title: Low or no water flow
common_problems.description: The purifier dispenses more slowly than usual or does not fill its storage tank.

common_problems.title: Change in taste or odour
common_problems.description: Water tastes or smells different; the cause cannot be determined from taste alone.

common_problems.title: Leak near the purifier
common_problems.description: Moisture appears at a connection, tap, tank or beneath the unit.

common_problems.title: Indicator, pump or sound concern
common_problems.description: A light, pump cycle or operating sound changes compared with normal use.

inspection_scope: Discuss the purifier model, filter-service history and the symptoms reported.
Inspect accessible tubing, connectors, tap, storage tank and indicators as appropriate.
Explain which components may need attention and list proposed consumables or parts clearly.
Confirm the scope with the customer before changing filters or performing additional work.

questions.question: Does a taste change prove that an RO filter needs replacement?
questions.answer: No. Taste or odour alone cannot verify water quality or identify a component failure. Follow the purifier manual and seek an appropriate inspection or water-quality test where needed.

questions.question: What information should I share about my purifier?
questions.answer: The brand and model, any indicator lights, approximate filter-service history, and when flow or taste changed can help frame the conversation.

questions.question: Will filter costs be shown separately?
questions.answer: A transparent estimate should identify proposed filter or other parts separately from inspection and labour, where applicable, before you decide.

title: Electrical Services
description: Review common household electrical concerns and understand how a qualified professional may inspect the affected circuit or fitting.
listing_description: Switches, sockets, lighting and circuit concerns that call for careful assessment.

common_problems.title: Breaker trips repeatedly
common_problems.description: A circuit switches off more than once or trips when a particular appliance is used.

common_problems.title: Flickering or dim lights
common_problems.description: One light or several lights flicker, dim or behave differently than usual.

common_problems.title: Switch or socket is not working
common_problems.description: A fitting has no power, feels loose or has visible damage.

common_problems.title: Heat, sparks or burning smell
common_problems.description: A potentially urgent warning sign around a fitting or electrical device.

inspection_scope: Discuss which fitting or circuit is affected and any visible warning signs.
Inspect the relevant accessible switch, socket, light or circuit using appropriate safety steps.
Explain findings and separate diagnostic work, labour and any proposed components.
Describe additional work and obtain customer approval before proceeding.

questions.question: What should I do if a socket smells burnt or sparks?
questions.answer: Do not touch a damaged fitting. If it is safe to do so, stop using the affected circuit and seek a qualified electrician promptly. In an immediate emergency, follow local emergency guidance.

questions.question: Can repeated breaker trips be ignored?
questions.answer: Repeated trips can indicate a problem and should not be bypassed. Avoid repeatedly resetting a breaker and arrange a qualified assessment.

questions.question: Will an electrical estimate list materials separately?
questions.answer: A clear proposal should describe the inspection, labour and any identified materials or fittings separately where practical, with scope changes explained for approval.

title: Plumbing Services
description: Explore everyday leak, drainage and water-flow concerns, plus the details a plumber may need before outlining a repair scope.
listing_description: Leaks, taps, drains, water pressure and other common household plumbing concerns.

common_problems.title: Tap or pipe is leaking
common_problems.description: Water drips from a tap, connection or visible pipe, sometimes only while in use.

common_problems.title: Slow or blocked drain
common_problems.description: Water drains slowly, backs up or leaves an unfamiliar odour near a fixture.

common_problems.title: Low or uneven water pressure
common_problems.description: One fixture or several fixtures have a noticeable change in water flow.

common_problems.title: Toilet keeps running
common_problems.description: The cistern continues to refill or water continues to move after flushing.

inspection_scope: Identify the affected fixture, when the issue occurs and whether water is still escaping.
Inspect accessible taps, traps, visible pipework and connections as appropriate.
Explain the proposed repair and distinguish labour from any materials or replacement parts.
Confirm customer approval before expanding the agreed scope or starting extra work.

questions.question: What information helps with a leak report?
questions.answer: Share where the water appears, when it happens, whether the source is visible and what fixtures are affected. If safe, turn off the relevant water supply while arranging help.

questions.question: Can every slow drain be cleared with a household chemical?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. Follow product and fixture guidance; mixing chemicals or using them on an unknown blockage can be hazardous. Describe the symptoms and seek an appropriate assessment.

questions.question: Will extra materials be charged without asking?
questions.answer: FixNear is being designed so proposed materials and scope changes are explained for customer approval before additional work proceeds.
